title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This leaf belongs to Grothendieck's notes for his 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. The neighbouring transcribed pages are SGA 7 Exposé IX typescript (Néron models, pairings on T_l), apparently reused as scrap paper, and are mathematically unrelated.

Setting.
- S is a commutative base ring.
- A_n = S{U_0,...,U_{n-1}}[dU_0,...,dU_{n-1}] is the PD de Rham algebra: the divided-power polynomial algebra in n variables, with its graded-commutative de Rham differential, d(U^{(j)}) = U^{(j-1)} dU.
- sigma_r^* : X_0 -> U_r are the coordinate (coface-type) maps from the one-variable algebra to the n-variable one. This is the shape of a cosimplicial or Čech–Alexander family A_n.
- A PD power series xi_i = sum_j a_{ij} X_0^{(j)} is given in one variable, with xi_{s,i} = sigma_s^*(xi_i).

The construction. Grothendieck wants to extend a map phi_n, already defined on the degree-0 generators by phi_n(U_r) = sigma_r^*(xi_1), to an S-algebra homomorphism A_n -> A_n. The images xi_{s,i} of the X_0^{(i)} are allowed to be non-homogeneous: xi_{s,i} = sum_j a_{ij} U_s^{(j)} + (sum_j b_{ij} U_s^{(j)}) dU_s.

He notes that it suffices to choose images of dU_0,...,dU_{n-1} and check three things: they square to zero, they anticommute with each other, and they commute with the xi_{s,i}. Compatibility with d forces
 phi(dU_r) = d sigma_r^*(xi_1) = (sum_{j>=1} a_{1j} U_r^{(j-1)}) dU_r.
These elements clearly square to zero and anticommute.

Commuting with xi_{s,i}:
- For s = r it is automatic, since dU_r^2 = 0.
- For s != r the odd parts anticommute, so one needs 2 (sum a_{1j} U_r^{(j-1)})(sum b_{ik} U_s^{(k)}) dU_r dU_s = 0.
- Hence the boxed condition: 2 a_{1j} b_{ik} = 0 for all j >= 1, k >= 0.
- The box then specialises a_{11} = 1 + sum alpha_i T^i with 2 alpha_i = 0, i.e. a deformation that is trivial away from 2-torsion.

So odd ('super') components in the images of even generators are only possible in 2-torsion or characteristic-2 situations.

The lemma. He then begins a general lemma to show that phi_n, a priori only an algebra homomorphism, commutes with d. Let A = S{U_0..U_m}[dU_0..dU_m], forgetting the PD structure except for the relation d U_r^{(i)} = U_r^{(i-1)} dU_r. Let B be an alternating dg S-algebra: graded commutative, odd squares zero, differential of degree +1. Study dg-homomorphisms f: A -> B. Presumably the statement is that an algebra map commuting with d on the generators U_r^{(i)} commutes with d everywhere, i.e. a universal property of the PD de Rham algebra. The page breaks off here.
errors: Only the commutation of phi(dU_r) with xi_{s,i} is checked. It is not checked that the non-homogeneous images xi_{s,i} commute among themselves (this needs 2 b_{ik} b_{i'k'} = 0 for s != t). Nor is it checked that they satisfy the divided-power relations (xi^{(a)} xi^{(b)} = binom(a+b,a) xi^{(a+b)}) needed for phi_n to be well defined on S{U}. Possibly this is handled on other pages.

The left-margin formula '2(sum b_ij U_s^{(j)})' omits the even factor (sum a_{1j} U_r^{(j-1)}) and the dU_r dU_s, which appear separately; it is a shorthand, not a real error. The derivative formulas themselves are correct.

ideas.what: PD de Rham dg-algebra of the divided-power polynomial algebra, with d(U^{(j)}) = U^{(j-1)} dU, and dg-homomorphisms out of it (universal property).
ideas.modern_name: PD de Rham complex / divided-power polynomial de Rham algebra (crystalline Poincaré lemma setting)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 1976 IHES lecture was not published as far as I know; unsure

ideas.what: Extending substitutions X_0 -> PD power series to endomorphisms of the multi-variable PD de Rham algebra, via coordinate maps sigma_r^* (cosimplicial structure).
ideas.modern_name: action of PD formal-line automorphisms on the cosimplicial (Čech–Alexander) PD de Rham algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in crystalline cohomology (Berthelot; Bhatt–de Jong Čech–Alexander complexes 2011)

ideas.what: Non-homogeneous ('odd-component') images of even generators allowed only under 2-torsion conditions (2 a_{1j} b_{ik} = 0, 2 alpha_i = 0).
ideas.modern_name: graded-commutativity sign constraints in characteristic 2 / super-endomorphisms of commutative dg-algebras

missed.claim: Grothendieck explores endomorphisms of the PD de Rham algebra that mix degrees (images of X_0^{(i)} with dU-components), finding that these exist only modulo 2-torsion. This is a characteristic-2 'super' phenomenon he starts to examine but does not develop on this page. It is minor and largely folklore.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is marginal. Char-2 phenomena for de Rham / derived de Rham complexes and the non-strictness of commutative dg-algebras in char 2 are of current interest, but this computation is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine working computations on the PD de Rham algebra: extending algebra maps, checking sign and commutation conditions, and the start of a standard universal-property lemma. The only slightly unusual feature is the char-2 non-homogeneous maps, which is elementary.
transcription_corrections: The neighbouring pages are SGA 7 Exp. IX typescript (likely the reverse side or a reused sheet), not a continuation of this manuscript.
'σ_r^H' is probably σ_r^* (pullback along the r-th coordinate map), consistent with 'ξ_{s,i} = σ_s^*(X_0^{(i)})' later.
The parenthetical reads roughly '(on néglige la structure de p.d., à au moins d U_r^{(i)} = U_r^{(i-1)} dU_r ...)'; the transcription's 'dU_r^{(i)}' should be d(U_r^{(i)}).
'Soit B une S-alg. diff. alternée (quand l. mod 2?), différentielle de degré +1)': the reading is uncertain but plausibly '(graduée mod 2)'.
